findings.title: Embed URL injected raw into HTML, enabling XSS in the rendered embed view
findings.body: The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into both the href attribute and the link text via I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}"). Imported posts are persisted with cook_method = :raw_html and the embed view renders their HTML through `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so the appended markup is emitted verbatim into the discourse origin. An embed URL containing a single quote, a newline, an `on*=` payload, or a `javascript:` scheme (originating from any RSS item, from a CMS at SiteSetting.embeddable_host, or from any direct caller of TopicEmbed.import) breaks out of the `` attribute and runs attacker-supplied HTML/JS. The call also mutates the caller's `contents` string in place via `<<`, which can break frozen-string inputs and corrupts the caller's data. Use Rails' link_to(url) (or html_escape) and build the suffix into a separate String instead of mutating `contents`.

findings.title: <%- end if %> is a SyntaxError in Ruby ERB and will prevent the embed view from rendering
findings.body: Line 6 closes the first if/else block with `  <%- end if %>`. Inside ERB that compiles to the literal Ruby `end if`, whose `if` modifier requires a condition expression. With no condition following `if`, Ruby's parser raises a SyntaxError the first time the view is compiled, so any request that reaches `best.html.erb` (i.e., any embedded topic that has been imported) will blow up instead of rendering. The other if/else in this same file (lines 11, 22, 29) closes with plain `<%- end %>`, confirming that this is a stray ` if` typo. Replace with `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a recognized directive
findings.body: The action unconditionally sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The only valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and the deprecated ALLOW-FROM <uri>. Browsers will silently ignore "ALLOWALL" and fall back to their default framing policy, so unless an equivalent Content-Security-Policy `frame-ancestors *` is set, the very framing that the embed feature was built to enable will be blocked in modern browsers. Use CSP `frame-ancestors *` (or remove this header and rely on CSP) instead.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf instead of a real origin comparison
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` only confirms that e.origin appears as a substring of discourseUrl. Any e.origin that is a substring of whatever `discourseUrl` is configured to (including future paths/queries/cached redirects) will pass the gate and be allowed to set `iframe.height` or drive other future message handlers. Use `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin` (or compare parsed origins via the postMessage API's own origin field) so the handler accepts only the configured Discourse origin.

findings.title: PollFeed job aborts the entire hourly run on the first item or network failure
findings.body: Inside the `rss.items.each` loop, `i.content.scrub` raises on a nil/Non-String item content, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` raises on any transient network or HTTP error, and `TopicEmbed.import` raises on URL-regex mismatch or Nokogiri errors from `absolutize_urls`. Combined with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one malformed item or one bad network response silently drops every subsequent item in the feed until the next hourly cron — and the exceptions are lost because the `feed_polling_enabled?` guard never runs around the loop. Wrap each item (and the open/parse) in begin/rescue, validate i.link/i.id/i.title/i.content up front, and log per-item errors so a single bad entry does not poison the entire run.

findings.title: feed_key helper is dead code
findings.body: The class defines `feed_key` (computing `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but never references it. Either wire it into the poll path (e.g., a per-feed HTTP If-Modified-Since/last-modified check, or a rate-limit key to avoid re-importing unchanged items) or remove the unused method to avoid the impression that per-feed change detection exists.

findings.title: request.referer is interpolated into a JS context without j/JS escaping
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` relies on Rails default HTML escaping inside a JavaScript string literal. While `'` happens to be escaped in a way that is inert inside a `<script>` block today, the correct helper for a value going into a JS string literal is `j request.referer` (or escaping explicitly for targetOrigin). The embed controller deliberately lets attacker-controllable URLs reach the referer header, so passing that value to postMessage's targetOrigin should be JS-escaped so that backslashes/control bytes produced by a hostile header cannot break the JS string or smuggle a different targetOrigin.

findings.title: Throttle uses non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE, which can leak a permanent key
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` leaves a brief window in which the key exists with no TTL. If the second command is lost (network blip, sidekiq preemption, Redis failover) the key has no expiry and permanently blocks retrievals for that URL. Use the atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` form instead.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import_remote (external URL fetch + ruby-readability) is not exercised
findings.body: import_remote performs `open(url).read`, runs ruby-readability with the specific tags/attributes allowlist, and forwards the result into import. It is the highest-risk entry point in this PR (SSRF surface, hang on slow hosts, content that ends up as raw_html posts) and is reachable from both TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the disqus.thor import task. The new spec only covers import(), so any regression in the allowlist, the host contract, or the read/open behaviour would slip through.

findings.title: poll_feed body (RSS item iteration, normalisation, TopicEmbed.import integration) is uncovered
findings.body: The new spec only verifies the three guard conditions in execute() (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url present, embed_by_username present). The actual poll_feed body that parses the feed, falls back from i.link to i.id, runs CGI.unescapeHTML + i.content.scrub, and calls TopicEmbed.import per item is the section this review flagged as fragile (nil item fields, scrub failures, regex mismatch on id fallback) and is not tested at all.
